# Actual first emissions and original native requests

Root executed the frozen first-emission driver on 2026-10-06 (Asia/Tokyo).
All four fixed existing CLI emissions, widths 0–3, completed with exit 0.
The fixed rejecting sentinel observed no native attempts. The source and four
independent requests were already frozen in `first-files.json`; none changed.
Emission produced untrusted IR, without a semantic check or execution probe.

After separate source and independent capture review, root executed exactly
eight original-payload operations: fresh inspect followed by unchanged request
at each width. [Raw records](original-native-capture-01/summary.json) retain all
eight client commands and real native process records. Every input was fully
written; no spawn, deadline, output-cap, identity or wrapper failure occurred.
Root separately checked every raw client/native byte count and recorded digest.

| Width | Original payload bytes | Fresh inspect | Structural / exact work | Unchanged request |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | 1,185 | accepted | 2,190 / 0 | native `contract`, exit 1 |
| 1 | 15,162 | accepted | 65,384 / 131 | native `contract`, exit 1 |
| 2 | 32,126 | accepted | 157,173 / 262 | native `contract`, exit 1 |
| 3 | 52,423 | accepted | 272,786 / 393 | native `contract`, exit 1 |

Each successful inspect retains the exact original payload, no request or
candidate, and no instrument. Each request has one recorded native process:
width zero uses composition-request mode; positive widths use Fourier-request
mode. Their strict raw frames contain `error/contract`. These are actual native
rejections, rather than Rust child-arity refusal or a hypothetical expected
result. The coarse frame itself does not identify a particular failed rule.

The original complete endpoints differ from the frozen canonical endpoints:
input owner 101 at every width; output owners 101,105,120,134 respectively;
positive output axis labels are reversed at widths two and three. Independent
requests keep owner 0, ordered canonical axes, exact Bits width and no classical
ports. Source inspection confirms that complete endpoint equality is required;
these first results do not test a canonically bound candidate's Fourier meaning.
The zero request remains the original single identity rewire on one Bits0 owner.
Neither it nor a positive request is replaced to fit the output.

Existing conditional Lean results already derive the inspected operator's exact
Fourier matrix and reference laws under the actual finite/H obligations. Native
packet/decoder/binary correspondence retains its stated assumptions. These new
observations provide no source-preservation, general family/resource proof,
QFT2/3 specialization equivalence or canonical std API. QS/PR/RS/EXACT broader
duties and the two admitted ordinary QLV1 scopes retain their original status.
All 111 targets and all 24 #317 criteria remain required; completion is still
14/111 (12.61%). No guarantee admission or release approval follows.

Next, separately reviewed phase-free bookkeeping routes may bind these outputs
to the unchanged canonical requests. They must retain child-position one, the
real ordered suffix/reversal, every finite body and exact phase; each resulting
untrusted artifact requires its own fresh inspect and request check. Original
first sources, outputs, requests and failures remain immutable.
